title: U.S. House · Maryland's 5th District
area: Southern Maryland and parts of Prince George's and Anne Arundel counties, including Waldorf, La Plata and Lexington Park.

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Steny Hoyer did not seek re-election. Adrian Boafo, a Maryland delegate, won a crowded 24-candidate Democratic primary. Chris Chaffee won the Republican primary over Bryan Duval Cubero and Michelle Talkington. Mildred Hall is also on the general-election ballot as a write-in candidate.

candidates.name: Adrian Boafo
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary in a field of more than 20 candidates.

summary.text: Adrian Boafo is the Democratic nominee for the open Maryland 5th Congressional District seat, which Rep. Steny Hoyer is leaving. A former Bowie city councilmember and mayor pro tem, he has served in the Maryland House of Delegates since 2023 and worked for Hoyer's campaigns and for Oracle Corporation in government affairs. He won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 32.7% of the vote in a field of more than 20 candidates.

background.text: Born in Arlington, Virginia, on May 10, 1994; graduated from DeMatha Catholic High School in 2012.
Earned a B.A. in government and public policy from the University of Baltimore in 2016 and an M.B.A. from American University's Kogod School of Business in 2019.

Early in his career he was a national press assistant for U.S. Rep. Ruben Kihuen (2017-2018), then field director (2018-2019) and campaign manager (2019-2021) for Steny Hoyer's congressional campaign.
Elected to the Bowie City Council (District 3) in 2019 and served as the city's mayor pro tem; he held both roles from 2019 to 2022, according to his legislative profile.
Has worked for Oracle Corporation since 2021, listed in his legislative profile as senior director of government affairs.

Won election to the Maryland House of Delegates from District 23 in 2022 and took office on January 11, 2023. He serves on the Economic Matters Committee, including its Workers' Compensation, Land Use and Zoning, and Business Regulation subcommittees.
Was a delegate to the 2024 Democratic National Convention, pledged to Kamala Harris, according to Wikipedia.
Announced his run for Congress on January 12, 2026; Hoyer endorsed him on January 23, 2026. He is not seeking re-election to the House of Delegates in 2026.

priorities.text: Affordability, including raising the federal minimum wage, cutting taxes for working families, and expanding the Child Tax Credit and Earned Income Tax Credit.
Guaranteeing universal childcare so parents do not have to choose between work and caring for their children.
Democracy and civil rights, including overturning Citizens United and passing the Equality Act and John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act.

positions.summary: Voted yes on SB 555, the Fair Wage Act of 2023, which accelerated Maryland's minimum wage to $15 an hour.

stated.summary: Wants to raise the federal minimum wage from $7.25 to $15 an hour and tie it to inflation, citing his work leading a three-year effort to raise Maryland's minimum wage.

positions.summary: Says he will guarantee universal childcare so no parent has to choose between earning a paycheck and caring for their child.
Voted yes on HB 352, the Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act of 2025, which created new state income-tax brackets and a capital-gains surtax on high earners.

stated.summary: Says he will cut taxes for working and middle-class families while closing loopholes that let large corporations and wealthy individuals avoid paying what he calls their fair share.

positions.summary: Voted yes on SB 1, the Gun Safety Act of 2023, which restricted where firearms may be carried and created new sensitive-location restrictions.

stated.summary: Says he will advance gun safety reforms to protect schools and children and invest in mental health services.

record.text: Led a three-year effort in the Maryland legislature to raise the state minimum wage and tie future increases to inflation.
Co-sponsored the Protection from Predatory Pricing Act of 2026 in the Maryland legislature.
Voted yes on SB 555 (Fair Wage Act of 2023, accelerating Maryland's minimum wage to $15 an hour), which passed the House of Delegates 102-38 on April 4, 2023.
Voted yes on SB 1 (Gun Safety Act of 2023, restricting where firearms may be carried and creating new sensitive-location restrictions), which passed the House of Delegates 93-42 on April 10, 2023.

Voted yes on HB 352 (Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act of 2025, creating new state income-tax brackets and a capital-gains surtax on high earners), which passed the House of Delegates 94-46 on April 7, 2025.

summary.text: Chris Chaffee is the Republican nominee for the open Maryland 5th Congressional District seat. According to Ballotpedia, he is a general contractor and farmer who has been a repeat candidate: the Republican nominee for this seat in 2014 and for U.S. Senate in 2022, and a candidate in the 2024 Senate primary. He won the June 23, 2026 Republican primary with 51.2% of the vote.

background.text: According to Ballotpedia, studied at Prince George's Community College and the University of Maryland; no degrees are listed.
Professional experience listed as general contractor and farmer.
Won the Republican nomination for Maryland's 5th District in 2014 and lost the general election to Rep. Steny Hoyer, 35.7% to 64%.
Won the 2022 Republican primary for U.S. Senate (20.8%) and lost the general election to Sen. Chris Van Hollen, receiving 34.1% of the vote.
Ran in the 2024 Republican primary for U.S. Senate, finishing third with 3.2% behind Larry Hogan and Robin Ficker.
Won the June 23, 2026 Republican primary for this seat with 51.2%, ahead of Michelle Talkington and Bryan Duval Cubero.

positions.summary: Said Congress should not act to protect abortion rights following the Supreme Court's 2022 Dobbs decision.
